title: Inlet NOx Sensor Drifted High
shortDescription: Upstream NOx sensor reading drifted above plausible limit.
fullDescription:
SPN 3216 monitors the inlet (engine-out) NOx sensor on Mack MP7/MP8/MP10 engines in Anthem, Pinnacle, and Granite trucks. FMI 20 = data drifted high. As NOx sensors age, the zirconia cell degrades and readings climb beyond true engine-out NOx — triggering SCR efficiency miscalculations.

Mack NOx sensors typically last 3-5 years / 500,000 miles. Replacement is straightforward but $600-$900 per sensor OEM. Recommend replacing inlet and outlet together to maintain matched aging.

Sensor drift often pairs with SPN 4364 (SCR efficiency) since the incorrect baseline throws off conversion math.

fixSteps.title: Confirm drift
fixSteps.instruction: With Mack Premium Tech Tool (PTT), monitor inlet NOx at idle — should be ~50-300 ppm. High at idle = drift.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor(s)
fixSteps.instruction: Allow exhaust cooldown. Use 22mm NOx socket. Apply anti-seize (not on sensing element). Torque to spec.

fixSteps.title: Relearn
fixSteps.instruction: Clear codes with PTT and drive cycle. New sensor may take 1-2 cycles to stabilize.

videoSearchQuery: Mack Anthem MP8 NOx sensor SPN 3216 replace

faq.a: Only on threads, never on sensing tip — will poison the cell.

title: DEF Pressure Sensor Voltage High
shortDescription: DEF supply pressure sensor signal above normal range.
fullDescription:
SPN 4334 FMI 3 on Mack MP7/MP8 engines points to the DEF (AdBlue) pressure sensor inside the DEF supply module. High voltage = open signal wire or failed sensor.

If the pressure reading is unreliable, the ECM cannot verify proper dosing, leading to derate inducement and companion SCR codes. Diagnose the sensor harness first, then the sensor.

Supply module sensor is often not serviceable separately on Mack/Volvo — full module swap required.

causes.cause: Failed pressure sensor in DEF supply module

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug DEF supply module harness, check for corrosion from road salt.

fixSteps.title: Test signal wire
fixSteps.instruction: Back-probe signal wire. Key on should read 0.5-4.5V based on pressure. 5V+ = open.

fixSteps.title: Replace DEF supply module
fixSteps.instruction: Drain DEF, unbolt module, swap, refill and prime via PTT.

videoSearchQuery: Mack Anthem DEF pressure sensor SPN 4334

faq.a: Usually no — supply module is one assembly.
OEM recommended due to programming compatibility.

title: Engine Speed Sensor 2 (Cam) Signal Abnormal
shortDescription: Camshaft position sensor signal intermittent or abnormal frequency.
fullDescription:
SPN 723 is the secondary engine speed sensor (camshaft sensor on Mack MP-series). FMI 8 = abnormal frequency or duty cycle — signal present but not right.

Crank/cam correlation is essential for injector timing. Lost cam signal forces the ECM into a default 'limp' fueling map or may cause no-start. Common failures: sensor gap drift from wear, metal debris on sensor tip, cracked tone wheel.

On Mack Anthem/Pinnacle with MP8, the sensor is in the front gear train area — access typically requires front cover work.

fixSteps.title: Clean sensor tip
fixSteps.instruction: Remove cam sensor, wipe metallic debris with clean rag. Measure air gap per spec.

fixSteps.title: Check signal
fixSteps.instruction: Use scope or frequency meter on sensor output while cranking. Should see clean pulse train.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new sensor with proper torque. Clear codes and verify with PTT.

whenToCallPro: If front cover service needed for tone wheel.
videoSearchQuery: Mack MP8 cam sensor SPN 723 replace

faq.a: Gear wear particles attracted to magnetic sensor — some is normal.
Mack runs on crank alone in limp — cam fault = rough run but may still start.

title: DPF Inlet Temperature Above Normal (Extreme)
shortDescription: DPF inlet exhaust temperature critically high — risk of DPF substrate damage.
fullDescription:
SPN 3242 FMI 0 flags DPF inlet exhaust temperature above safe limits (often >1200°F / 650°C). On Mack MP7/MP8, this is typically caused by an uncontrolled regen — excess dosing, DPF heavily loaded, or DOC substrate failure.

If left unchecked, DPF substrate can melt/crack, requiring $5,000+ replacement. A stuck-open EGR or failed dosing system can also contribute. Engine derate activates to protect hardware.

After an over-temp event, inspect DPF for substrate damage via borescope before returning to service.

fixSteps.title: Shut down
fixSteps.instruction: Pull safely off road, shut down engine. Do not stop over flammable material.

fixSteps.title: Inspect DPF temp sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Verify temp readings with PTT. If wildly different from outlet sensors, suspect inlet sensor fault.

fixSteps.title: Inspect DPF substrate
fixSteps.instruction: Dealer borescope inspection. Replace if melted or cracked.

videoSearchQuery: Mack MP8 SPN 3242 FMI 0 DPF over temperature

faq.a: No — substrate is ceramic, cracks are terminal.
High Exhaust System Temp — normal during regen, concerning if extreme.

title: EGR Delta Pressure Slightly High
shortDescription: EGR venturi pressure drop elevated — early sign of sooting.
fullDescription:
SPN 411 FMI 15 (least severe) on Mack MP7/MP8 indicates EGR venturi pressure drop is beginning to exceed normal. Early warning — clean now, before it escalates to FMI 0 and derate.

Delta-pressure sample tubes clogging with soot is the single most common cause, not a real restriction. Blow out tubes first; typically resolves the code. Full EGR cleaning follows if needed.

Schedule EGR service at this warning rather than waiting for power loss.

fixSteps.title: Blow out DP tubes
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect small metal tubes from DP sensor and venturi ports. Blow clear with compressed air.

fixSteps.title: Clear and test
fixSteps.instruction: Clear code with PTT. Drive cycle — if returns, full EGR cleaning needed.

fixSteps.title: EGR cleaning
fixSteps.instruction: Pull EGR valve and venturi, clean carbon with intake cleaner and brass brush. Reinstall with new gaskets.

whenToCallPro: If access difficult or cooler service needed.
videoSearchQuery: Mack MP8 EGR DP sensor clean SPN 411

faq.a: Yes — hair-sized soot bits restrict flow and give false high readings.

title: DPF Soot Load Moderate — Regen Needed
shortDescription: DPF soot approaching derate threshold — perform parked regen.
fullDescription:
SPN 3251 FMI 16 on Mack MP7/MP8 indicates DPF soot above moderate threshold. Not yet 5 mph derate but escalating. A parked regen should clear it.

Mack Anthem/Pinnacle use dash-initiated regen: set parking brake, neutral, high idle, press regen switch. Expect 30-45 minutes. Do not park over combustibles — regen exhaust exceeds 1100°F.

Frequent regen needs typically indicate short-haul duty cycle, low-load operation, or a failing dosing/DOC system.

fixSteps.title: Parked regen
fixSteps.instruction: Park safely, set brake and neutral, initiate regen via dash switch. 30-45 min.

fixSteps.title: Follow with highway run
fixSteps.instruction: After regen, run 55+ mph for 30 min to establish passive regen baseline.

fixSteps.title: Service dosing if repeats
fixSteps.instruction: If code returns quickly, test dosing injector flow with PTT.

whenToCallPro: If regen won't initiate or completes repeatedly.
videoSearchQuery: Mack Anthem parked regen SPN 3251 FMI 16

faq.a: It restarts from the beginning — wastes fuel and time.

title: DEF Heater Not Responding Properly
shortDescription: DEF tank or line heater failing to warm DEF in cold ambient.
fullDescription:
SPN 3363 covers the DEF tank/line heater circuit. FMI 7 = not responding — ECM commanded heating but DEF temperature did not rise as expected.

DEF freezes at 12°F; without heaters, the system cannot dose. On Mack MP7/MP8 trucks, heaters include a tank immersion heater and heated supply/return lines. Any of these can fail due to coolant loop loss, wiring, or thermostat.

Without working heater, truck derates in winter after a short grace window.
symptoms: DEF dosing faults at cold start

fixSteps.title: Verify coolant loop
fixSteps.instruction: Check coolant loop to DEF tank — feel lines hot after warm-up. Bleed air if needed.

fixSteps.title: Test heater resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect and measure heater coil resistance per service spec. Open = replace.

fixSteps.title: Replace component
fixSteps.instruction: Replace failed line or tank heater. OEM parts recommended.

videoSearchQuery: Mack DEF heater SPN 3363 FMI 7 winter

faq.a: Usually 20 minutes before ECM flags heater fault.
In emergency yes, but underlying heater fault still needs repair.

title: AHI Fuel Shut-Off Valve Not Responding
shortDescription: Aftertreatment fuel shut-off valve stuck or not moving when commanded.
fullDescription:
SPN 3482 FMI 7 on Mack MP7/MP8 engines monitors the AHI (Aftertreatment Hydrocarbon Injection) fuel shut-off valve that controls supply to the 7th injector dosing system.

The valve opens to admit fuel for regen dosing, closes otherwise to prevent coking in the dosing line. If stuck, regen either can't start or keeps flowing fuel when it shouldn't.

Common failures: varnish buildup from poor fuel quality, coil failure, or mechanical stick after long storage periods.

fixSteps.title: Actuation test
fixSteps.instruction: Command valve open/close via PTT and listen/feel for click. No click = likely coil or harness.

fixSteps.title: Check harness
fixSteps.instruction: Measure coil resistance and harness continuity.

fixSteps.title: Replace valve
fixSteps.instruction: Swap valve, clean any coking, re-prime regen fuel line via PTT.

videoSearchQuery: Mack AHI fuel shutoff valve SPN 3482

faq.a: Aftertreatment Hydrocarbon Injection — dosing for regen.
Quality fuel, biocide additives in slow-turn fleets.

title: Engine Overspeed
shortDescription: Engine RPM exceeded maximum — possible runaway or downshift over-rev.
fullDescription:
SPN 190 FMI 0 flags engine RPM above the governor's absolute limit. On Mack MP7/MP8 this threshold is typically 2300-2500 RPM depending on configuration.

Causes include driver downshifting too aggressively downhill (overrunning engine with transmission), runaway engine (blow-by oil feeding combustion), or tach sensor noise.

A true runaway from crankcase oil ingestion is an emergency — engine will accelerate uncontrollably and can fly apart. Emergency shutdown procedure: block air intake with heavy material or activate air shutoff valve if equipped.

fixSteps.title: Retrieve freeze frame
fixSteps.instruction: With PTT, pull freeze frame data. If truck in high RPM while coasting or decelerating — driver downshift event.

fixSteps.title: Rule out runaway
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect CCV/breather for heavy oil mist. Check turbo for shaft play and oil seal leak. Oil-fed runaway is catastrophic.

fixSteps.title: Sensor check if no cause found
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect crank/cam sensors for chipped tone wheel or debris.

videoSearchQuery: Mack MP8 SPN 190 FMI 0 engine overspeed diagnose

faq.a: Block air intake with jacket or floor mat. Diesel needs air — cut it and engine dies.
Usually harmless if RPM was brief — monitor for other damage.

title: Turbo Boost Pressure Very High
shortDescription: Boost pressure above max — VGT stuck closed or wastegate fault.
fullDescription:
SPN 1127 FMI 0 indicates intake boost has exceeded the ECM's maximum safe limit on Mack MP7/MP8 engines. Usually caused by a VGT with stuck-closed vanes (maximum boost) or a failed VGT actuator holding max position.

Overboost risk: cracked piston, bent rods, blown head gasket. ECM derates immediately when detected.

A common secondary cause is a disconnected or leaking boost reference line giving the ECM wrong data.

causes.cause: VGT vanes stuck closed / actuator hung

fixSteps.title: Actuate VGT via PTT
fixSteps.instruction: Command VGT 0-100% — watch actual position track command. If stuck, remove turbo for vane cleaning.

fixSteps.title: Verify sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Cross-check boost sensor vs known-good mechanical gauge.

fixSteps.title: Service VGT
fixSteps.instruction: Remove turbo, clean carbon off vanes, or replace actuator. Recalibrate via PTT.

title: Ambient Air Temperature Sensor Voltage Low
shortDescription: Ambient air temperature sensor circuit shorted to ground.
fullDescription:
SPN 171 FMI 4 on Mack Anthem/Pinnacle indicates the ambient temperature sensor circuit is shorted to ground — ECM reads implausibly cold temperature. Affects DEF heater strategy, cold-start fueling, and display.

Often just a chafed harness where the sensor wiring passes through grommets. Sensor itself rarely fails — usually a wiring issue.

Fix is inexpensive but requires tracing harness.

fixSteps.title: Inspect sensor connector
fixSteps.instruction: Check for water or corrosion. Dry and reassemble with dielectric grease.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect and test
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug sensor — if code changes to FMI 3 (open), sensor is likely the short. Measure resistance.

fixSteps.title: Repair harness or replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Repair chafed wire with solder/heat shrink or replace sensor.

whenToCallPro: If not comfortable with harness repair.

faq.a: Rarely, but affects DEF and cold-start strategy.

title: Adaptive Cruise Radar Data Erratic
shortDescription: Bendix/Wabco adaptive cruise radar returning erratic data — dirty sensor or misalignment.
fullDescription:
SPN 1590 FMI 2 on Mack Anthem and Pinnacle equipped with Bendix Wingman Fusion or Wabco adaptive cruise indicates the forward radar is producing erratic data. Typically caused by a dirty radar cover, misalignment from a grille bump, or a wiring issue.

The system disables adaptive cruise and collision mitigation when this sets. Safe to drive but advanced safety features are inactive.

Aftermarket plastic bumper damage or winter ice buildup are frequent culprits. Alignment requires a dealer target procedure.

fixSteps.title: Clean radar
fixSteps.instruction: Locate radar behind front grille. Clean cover gently with damp cloth.

fixSteps.title: Verify alignment
fixSteps.instruction: Visually check that radar is firmly mounted and level. If bumped, dealer alignment with target board needed.

fixSteps.title: Replace radar
fixSteps.instruction: Dealer procedure if diagnostic confirms radar unit failure.
